about.title: Gardena Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Gardena residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Los Angeles County hospital systems for care, and most of the time that care goes as expected. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication dosing, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — there are strict notice requirements, shorter windows to act, and rules limiting certain damages that don't apply elsewhere. A bad outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the law requires showing the provider deviated from an accepted standard of care. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your medical records — we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened and explain your options, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: California generally requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the healthcare provider before a malpractice case can be filed, and the underlying claim itself is usually limited to one year from discovery, capped at three years from the injury. Missing either window can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Damage Caps Change Over Time
items.desc: MICRA sets a cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but that cap rises each year under current law. An attorney can explain how the cap applies to your specific timeline and circumstances.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California generally requires a qualified medical expert to establish that a provider's care fell below the accepted standard. An independent attorney can help arrange the kind of medical review these claims typically need.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Gardena?
items.answer: California law generally gives you one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before filing suit. Because these deadlines can overlap in confusing ways, it helps to talk to an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves risk, and an unexpected or poor result doesn't by itself mean a provider did anything wrong. California requires showing the provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, which is why a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to evaluate the case.

items.question: Does LawProactive handle malpractice claims for people in Gardena directly?
items.answer: No — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't provide legal advice or evaluate medical records ourselves. We simply help Gardena residents connect with an independent attorney in our network who handles medical malpractice matters and works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.
